Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Working diagnosis: Viral upper respiratory tract infection / influenza
- Key clinical findings, reasoning, and impressions:
  - Acute onset of sore throat, nasal congestion with clear discharge, dry cough, fatigue over ~4 days
  - Initial fever that has since subsided with paracetamol/ibuprofen
  - Night sweats and exertional dyspnea on activity but not at rest
  - No chest pain or significant dyspnea at rest; symptoms largely self-limited
  - History consistent with a viral process; clinician stated assessment of viral URI or early influenza
- Relevant differentials from DDx that support/refine impression:
  - Viral upper respiratory tract infection / influenza (High)
  - Acute bronchitis (Medium)
  - Streptococcal pharyngitis (Medium-Low)
- Considerations:
  - Allergic rhinitis possible but systemic/fever symptoms favor infectious etiology
- Plan:
  - Self-care for viral illness: restful activities, adequate fluids, and continued use of acetaminophen/ibuprofen as needed
  - Return-to-work guidance: consider taking a day or two off; return when feeling better
  - Red flags requiring earlier review: high fever, worsening shortness of breath, chest pain, or inability to manage symptoms
  - Antibiotics not indicated unless bacterial infection suspected or symptoms worsen significantly

- Education on chronic disease prevention and lifestyle modification: Provided general guidance on rest, fluids, and symptomatic care; monitor for red flags
- Patient health goals and priorities: Return to usual functioning and work when symptomatic relief is achieved

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

- Viral upper respiratory tract infection / influenza
  - Likelihood: High
  - Justification: Acute onset of sore throat, clear nasal discharge, congestion, dry cough, fatigue, initial fever resolving; exposure to a sick contact; self-limited course typical of viral URI/influenza
- Acute bronchitis (viral or post-viral)
  - Likelihood: Medium
  - Justification: Cough developing after URI with mild exertional dyspnea; fits bronchitic pattern after a viral illness
- Streptococcal pharyngitis (GAS pharyngitis)
  - Likelihood: Low to Medium-Low
  - Justification: Odynophagia and prior fever present; nasal symptoms favor viral etiology; absence of classic exudates or tender cervical nodes lowers likelihood
